purpose: Limits the number of consecutive failed logon attempts, protecting against brute-force and credential-guessing attacks.
summary: The system enforces a defined threshold of failed logon attempts within a defined time period, after which it takes an automatic action such as locking the account or delaying further attempts.
expectedStatementElements: The time window the threshold applies to
The automatic action taken (lockout duration, delay, alert)
How the account is unlocked (self-service, help desk, timed)
Whether the setting is enforced system-wide or varies by system
evidenceExamples: System configuration showing the lockout threshold and duration
Screenshots of the account lockout policy setting
commonGaps: Statement says lockout is 'enabled' without stating the threshold or duration
No description of the unlock process
Setting not confirmed to be consistent across all in-scope systems
interviewQuestions: What is the exact failed-attempt threshold and lockout duration configured?
How does a user regain access after being locked out?
Is this setting consistent across every system in scope, or does it vary?
